title: A space billiards game built around gravity
author: skbphy
selftext:
I've been working on a small space game for a while. It basically plays like billiards: you launch a small black hole, use its gravity to change the direction of planets, and try to get them into black hole pockets. The main difference is that instead of hitting the planets directly, you're moving them with gravity.

I wrote a bit below about how I made it, the tools I used, and some of the simple mistakes I made along the way.

I started it as a learning project before attempting a much bigger game I have in mind. The first version leaned much more into the science side, with orbits, gravity and movement being the main focus, but it was honestly pretty boring to play. I gradually pushed it toward a more arcade-like structure. It still might not be that good, but it's definitely better than the early versions.

I also made the mistake of going too far with VFX early on. If something looked nice, I added it. Since I left optimization until much later, I ended up removing or simplifying a lot of those effects.

For 3D I used Tripo and Meshy. I eventually removed everything I made with Meshy because, even with the same reference images, I struggled to keep a consistent visual style between assets. Tripo was much better for that. I used Blender for cleanup and smaller fixes. I also made the music with Suno.

The game is built with Three.js, and I used 5.6 Sol and Fable 5.0 for coding. One of the stranger problems I ran into was language models treating intentional mechanics as bugs. I would deliberately make something less physically correct because it was more fun, then later the model would notice it and "fix" it back into the more boring version.

After this happened a few times, I started keeping important development decisions in md files and adding comments directly into the code explaining why certain behavior was intentional. That helped stop the same things from being "fixed" again later.

I also struggled a lot with things like level layouts, accessory placement and HUD design. Even when I tried to explain them visually, language models weren't very good at getting the exact result I wanted. So instead of constantly prompting for tiny changes, I had editor pages made for those systems and started adjusting positions, scale and layouts manually.

The project eventually grew to 100 levels with different characters and abilities, but I still mostly see it as a learning project. I'm still learning, still changing things, and I'm continuing to work on the game as I go. Any feedback welcome!

You can play it here:  
[itch.io](https://skbv0.itch.io/one-more-planet)

comments.author: yaosio
